camps.name: Helen Lake
camps.why: The standard high camp: it cuts the summit day to about 4,400 ft of climbing, but it is snow-covered and windy, and sites fill up on weekends.

camps.name: Horse Camp
camps.why: Sheltered, with a spring and trees, and a gentler first day. It leaves a longer summit push and a heavier haul over snow to the Gulch.

plan_conflict: Horse Camp is filed as a main camp, but the plan walks past it to Helen Lake on day 1, so Helen Lake is the single main camp for night 1.

camps.name: Timberline below the Hayden Glacier
camps.why: A bench at the foot of North and Middle Sister, so day 2 starts right at the North Sister climb and the exit down to Pole Creek is short.

camps.name: Camp Lake
camps.why: Reliable water but windy, with few sites, and it sits on the South Sister side. Better for a South and Middle only trip or a night before the traverse starts.

plan_conflict: Camp Lake is filed as the main camp and the Hayden Glacier bench as an exit camp, but a traverse that finishes with North Sister on day 2 sleeps at the Hayden bench on night 1.

new_camps.name: Middle Chain Lake camp
new_camps.why: The usual first night: a long day from Stevens Pass ends in a lake basin right below Bullseye Pass, so Bulls Tooth is a short start away.
new_camps.permit: Alpine Lakes Wilderness permit required for overnight stays.
new_camps.notes: Reached by the PCT, Icicle Creek and Chain Lakes trails, about 10 miles. Camp well back from the shore.

new_camps.name: Frosty Pass area camp
new_camps.why: Sleeping near Frosty Pass after the Bulls Tooth day leaves a shorter final walk down to Whitepine; exact sites vary by party and by snow.
new_camps.water: Check snowmelt or tarns near the pass.
new_camps.permit: Alpine Lakes Wilderness permit required for overnight stays.
new_camps.notes: This night is not firmly confirmed; some parties stay at the Chain Lakes again before crossing Frosty Pass.

camps.name: Chiwaukum Chain Lakes
camps.why: The only camp that makes sense: a lake basin about a mile from Bullseye Pass, so you sleep here both before and after the scramble.

new_camps.name: Holden Pass camp
new_camps.why: The high camp most parties use for Bonanza: it saves about 1,000 ft on summit day and puts the upper route within reach, at the cost of a rough hillside traverse.
new_camps.water: Snowmelt and small streams near the pass.
new_camps.permit: Glacier Peak Wilderness camping rules apply.
new_camps.notes: Reached by the Holden Lake trail and a faint climbers path. Bugs are heavy in midsummer. Some parties stay at Holden Lake instead.

camps.name: Holden Pass
camps.why: Saves about 1,000 ft of climbing on summit day and puts you at the glacier edge, but the climbers trail is faint and bugs are heavy.

camps.name: Holden Lake
camps.why: Easier to reach, with water and a good trail, but buggy and a longer summit day. Choose it for a slower pace or a late start.

camps.name: Holden Village ballfield campground
camps.why: A flat field a mile above the village, used the night before or after for a ferry connection. Too far for a normal night on this plan.

camps.name: Bivy below the waterfall slabs
camps.why: A rough ledge above Holden Pass for parties wanting an even shorter summit day; exposed and cramped, so most stop lower.

plan_conflict: Holden Pass and Holden Lake are both filed as main camps; the plan's high camp is Holden Pass, so Holden Lake is the other option for those nights.

camps.name: Holden Pass and the slab bivies above
camps.why: The higher camp trims a lot off summit day and sits under the buttress approach, but the way to it is brushy and the sites are small.

camps.name: Holden Lake
camps.why: Easy walking, water and roomy sites make this the comfortable base, though insects are bad and the summit day is longer.

camps.name: Holden Village
camps.why: A bed and meals before or after the climb, but it is 3,200 ft and many miles from the route, so it is not a camp for this plan.

camps.name: Holden Ballpark Campground
camps.why: A cheap option near the village trailhead for the night before an early start; exposed and few sites, and too low for the climb itself.

plan_conflict: Holden Pass and Holden Lake are both filed as main camps; the plan's high camp is Holden Pass, so Holden Lake is the other option for those nights.

camps.name: Swamp Creek Camp — the base for Needle Peak, Mount Lyall and Lyall Ridge
camps.why: The closest established camp to the Swamp Creek way trail, so the climbing day starts at the turnoff and the walk out is shorter.

camps.name: Fivemile Camp, Agnes Creek
camps.why: Closer to the road end and easier to reach, but it adds about two hours to summit day. Use it if the boat or shuttle runs late.

camps.name: Purple Point and Harlequin — the landing camps, and the boat that decides the trip
camps.why: Lake Chelan landing camps, used the night before when the boat schedule makes you miss the trailhead. Not on a normal two-day plan.

camps.name: High Bridge Camp — the shuttle terminus and the base for McGregor Mountain
camps.why: A shuttle stop near the trailhead for the night before or after. It is too low and too far from Needle Peak to be a climbing camp.

camps.name: High camp near North Star-Bonanza pass (~7,100 ft)
camps.why: Puts the north face a couple of hours away, with snowmelt water and exposed bivy sites, but it is a long haul with full packs.

camps.name: Holden Village
camps.why: Indoor sleeping and meals before the approach or after the exit; not a place to sleep during this climb.

camps.name: Holden Ballpark Campground
camps.why: A low-cost field camp a mile above the village for parties arriving the night before; exposed and without shelter, and too far to climb from.

camps.name: Entiat Meadows camp (5,100' clearing)
camps.why: The only practical base: the end of a long trail walk, with water close by and the big south slope above, so summit day is a short round trip.

camps.name: Chiwawa Basin high camp benches
camps.why: Flat heather benches below the snowfield, with melt water, so summit day is short; the approach is steep and sites are exposed.

camps.name: Phelps Creek Campground and the Chiwawa River road campgrounds
camps.why: A car camp for the night before, after the long rough drive up the Chiwawa River road. It gives an early start but is not a climbing camp.

camps.name: Lyman Lakes and Cloudy Pass
camps.why: Water, established sites and the peak's base all in one place, so summit day is a scramble from camp, but it is a long first day over Spider Gap.

camps.name: Spider Meadow and Phelps Basin
camps.why: A shorter first day with excellent camping, and you cross Spider Gap on day 2 with a lighter morning; it makes the climb a longer push.

camps.name: Phelps Creek Campground and the Chiwawa River road campgrounds
camps.why: A trailhead car camp for the night before after the long gravel drive; gives an earlier start but is nowhere near the peak.

camps.name: Copper Creek basin camp
camps.why: The high camp under the glacier, about 3 miles above the road, with water and a short summit day, but a steep approach with a full pack.

camps.name: Holden Village
camps.why: Indoor beds and meals before or after the climb, and a low start of 3,200 ft. It adds a long day if you sleep there between nights.

camps.name: Holden Ballpark Campground
camps.why: A field camp near the village for the night before an early start. Open and exposed with few sites, and far below the climb.

camps.name: Swamp Creek Camp — the base for Needle Peak, Mount Lyall and Lyall Ridge
camps.why: The established camp at the Swamp Creek turnoff; summit day starts here and returns here, which keeps the packs light and the brush short.

camps.name: Upper Swamp Creek basin
camps.why: Puts the Dark Glacier in view and shortens summit day, but it is brushy, slow to reach and has few good sites. Used by parties moving up.

camps.name: Fivemile Camp, Agnes Creek
camps.why: A shorter first day on the trail, with about two extra hours added to summit day. Good if the boat is late.

camps.name: Purple Point and Harlequin — the landing camps, and the boat that decides the trip
camps.why: Lake landing camps used when the boat connection fails; not part of a normal 3-day plan.

camps.name: High Bridge Camp — the shuttle terminus and the base for McGregor Mountain
camps.why: A shuttle stop near the trailhead for the night before or after; too low to start the climb from.

plan_conflict: Swamp Creek Camp and Upper Swamp Creek basin are both filed as main; the plan's summit-and-return day works from Swamp Creek Camp, so the upper basin is an option only.

camps.name: Lower Phelps Basin Bivy
camps.why: Sits right below the climb, so summit day is short, but sites are few and dry in late season; carry water from the creek.

camps.name: Spider Meadow and Phelps Basin
camps.why: Plenty of flat, protected sites with water about 5 miles in, which leaves a longer summit day. Go here if you want comfort over a short push.

camps.name: Phelps Creek Campground and the Chiwawa River road campgrounds
camps.why: A trailhead car camp for the night before after the rough gravel drive; it gives a morning start but is not a climbing camp.

plan_conflict: Lower Phelps Basin Bivy and Spider Meadow are both filed as main; the plan's upper-basin camp matches the bivy, so Spider Meadow is the alternative.

camps.name: Chiwawa Basin bench
camps.why: A flat heather bench near the col, with melt water; it makes the east ridge a short day, though it is windy and a long haul with packs.

camps.name: Phelps Creek Campground and the Chiwawa River road campgrounds
camps.why: A car camp for the night before after the long gravel drive; gives an earlier start but is nowhere near the ridge.

camps.name: Buck Creek Pass
camps.why: The popular camp at the top of the trail, with water, many sites and views, but a mile and some climbing from the start of the scramble.

camps.name: Basin below Pass No Pass
camps.why: The closest camp to the southwest face, so summit day is shorter; sites are fewer and it is a mile off the main trail.

camps.name: Phelps Creek Campground and the Chiwawa River road campgrounds
camps.why: A car camp on the far side of the range, used only if you reach Fortress from the Chiwawa; it gives no help with this approach.

plan_conflict: Buck Creek Pass and the Pass No Pass basin are both filed as main; the plan's title names Buck Creek Pass, so the basin is the other option.

new_camps.name: Upper Phelps Basin camp
new_camps.why: Puts the Dumbell col within reach for a short summit day, and the creek is close, but sites are few and small.
new_camps.permit: Glacier Peak Wilderness camping rules apply.
new_camps.notes: About 7 miles from the Phelps Creek trailhead. Some parties stay lower at Spider Meadow for more room and a longer summit day.
